title: Camera Path Spline Keyframe Editor
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive camera path spline keyframe editor. The scene should work as follows:

## Scene Setup
- A 3D environment with a ground plane (50x50, gray color) and a grid helper.
- Place 5 colored landmark objects in the scene: a red cube at (10,1,0), a green sphere at (-8,1,8), a blue cylinder at (5,1,-10), a yellow cone at (-12,1,-5), and a magenta torus at (0,1,12). These serve as visual reference points.
- Use an OrbitControls-enabled perspective camera starting at position (0, 20, 30) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light from (10,20,10).

## Spline Keyframe System
- Maintain an ordered list of keyframes. Each keyframe stores: position (Vector3), lookAt target (Vector3), and a time value (seconds, starting from 0).
- Start with 2 default keyframes: KF0 at position (0,5,20) lookAt (0,0,0) time=0, and KF1 at position (20,8,0) lookAt (0,0,0) time=3.
- Visualize keyframe positions as small orange spheres (radius 0.4) in the scene.
- Connect keyframes with a CatmullRomCurve3 spline, rendered as a yellow line (200 segments). Update the spline whenever keyframes change.
- Show a small green sphere (radius 0.3) as the 'playhead' indicator that moves along the spline during playback.

## UI Panel (DOM)
- Create a fixed panel on the left side (width 280px, dark background, white text, scrollable).
- Display a list of all keyframes showing index, position (x,y,z rounded to 1 decimal), and time.
- Highlight the currently selected keyframe in the list with a bright border.
- Buttons: 'Add Keyframe' (adds a new keyframe at the camera's current position/lookAt with time = last keyframe time + 2), 'Delete Keyframe' (removes selected, minimum 2 keyframes required), 'Play' (starts playback animation), 'Stop' (stops and resets playhead to start), 'Update Selected' (updates selected keyframe position to current camera position).
- A slider labeled 'Scrub' (range 0 to total duration, step 0.01) that moves the playhead along the spline and updates the green sphere position.
- A text input for editing the selected keyframe's time value, with an 'Apply Time' button.

## Interactions
- Click on a keyframe sphere in the 3D viewport (raycasting) to select it. The selected keyframe sphere turns red.
- Press 'N' key to add a new keyframe (same as Add Keyframe button).
- Press 'Delete' key to delete selected keyframe.
- Press 'Space' key to toggle play/stop.
- During playback, interpolate camera position along the CatmullRom spline based on keyframe times. The playhead (green sphere) follows the spline. Playback uses linear time interpolation between keyframe time values. The actual scene camera does NOT move during playback (user keeps orbit control); only the playhead moves.
- Playback automatically stops when reaching the last keyframe time.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields, updated every frame:
- keyframeCount: number of keyframes
- selectedKeyframeIndex: index of selected keyframe (-1 if none)
- keyframes: array of objects {x, y, z, time} for each keyframe (positions rounded to 2 decimals)
- splinePointCount: number of points in the rendered spline line geometry
- isPlaying: boolean, true during playback
- playheadTime: current playhead time in seconds (rounded to 2 decimals)
- playheadPosition: {x, y, z} of the green playhead sphere (rounded to 2 decimals)
- totalDuration: total duration (time of last keyframe, rounded to 2 decimals)
- scrubValue: current value of the scrub slider (rounded to 2 decimals)
- selectedKeyframeColor: hex color string of the selected keyframe sphere (e.g. '#ff0000') or null
- splineCurveType: string, should be 'catmullrom'
- lastAction: string describing last action taken ('add', 'delete', 'select', 'play', 'stop', 'scrub', 'updatePosition', 'applyTime', 'none')
physics_constraints: Spline interpolation must be continuous (no NaN positions). Keyframe times must be monotonically increasing. Playhead position must always lie on the spline curve. Minimum 2 keyframes enforced at all times. Scrub slider and playhead must stay synchronized.
